capacidades.p1.t02: The right capability at every step
capacidades.p1.t03: What your customers can do, what your team manages, and what supports risk assessment at every stage of lending.
capacidades.p1.t04: Origination · identification · calculations and decisioning · execution and documentation · collateral · disbursement and collections · operations · composition
capacidades.p1.t06: Customers need a clear path from offer to tracking; your team needs to know what to assess, execute, and authorize at each step. This catalog starts with that work and presents the capabilities that support it.
capacidades.p1.t10: A clear path for every application
capacidades.p1.t11: Composition creates value when specialized components serve the same journey. This is our interpretation of Gartner's emphasis on reuse.<sup class="fn">1</sup>
capacidades.p1.t12: Receivables financing for individuals and businesses
capacidades.p1.t13: Individuals and businesses access receivables financing through an offer, acceptance, and a signed assignment; the desk authorizes disbursement through Pix.
capacidades.p1.t15: Customers submit supporting documents, run a simulation, review the offer, and accept in the app. They track their application under “Em andamento” (In progress).
capacidades.p1.t17: For receivables financing, customers move through the offer, simulation, proposal, and acceptance in the app. The API channel connects that journey to credit assessment.
capacidades.p1.t19: Customers can also access their mobile journeys on desktop.
capacidades.p1.t21: Your customers recognize your brand and domain throughout the banking experience.
capacidades.p2.t03: Onboarding brings together identity, representation, and evidence. The FSB calls for attribution and traceability of AI agent actions.<sup class="fn">4</sup>
capacidades.p2.t05: Individuals open an account with their details, terms, and a motion selfie. Business onboarding brings owners and representatives into the same journey, with a review of formation documents.
capacidades.p2.t07: The applicant completes a live, gesture-based liveness check; the facial record forms part of the identity evidence.
capacidades.p2.t09: Customers receive an account-opening or sign-in code through the official WhatsApp account.
capacidades.p2.t11: Onboarding checks CPF taxpayer registration status and flags accounts requiring a registration update.
capacidades.p2.t13: Business onboarding, a motion selfie, and a code sent through WhatsApp.
capacidades.p3.t03: Applicants need an offer with clear amounts and terms. Risk teams need an identifiable policy and a reviewable decision path for every assessment.
capacidades.p3.t08: A trace of every rule applied.
capacidades.p3.t11: Customers review the discount, IOF (financial transactions tax), total effective cost (CET), and payment schedule to understand the terms. Your team can use Price, SAC, and BULLET calculations to structure the offer.
capacidades.p3.t13: Your risk team expresses policy in versioned decision tables, connects data sources, and reviews the path to the outcome. This provides context for examining the rule applied in each assessment.
capacidades.p3.t15: When a credit bureau response is still pending, the application is routed to a person for review. The desk keeps the credit assessment moving.
capacidades.p3.t18: Article 36 of Anexo Normativo II (Normative Annex II) to Resolução CVM nº 175 (Brazilian investment fund regulation), December 23, 2022, establishes the fund manager's duty to verify underlying receivables.<sup class="fn">5</sup> This context informs the role of the records shown alongside.
capacidades.p3.t20: Customers receive an email invitation and confirm their signature with a code; your team can review the sealed PDF and completion certificate.
capacidades.p3.t22: An assignment transaction with linked counterparties opens once the signature has been verified, connecting workflow progression to verified execution.
capacidades.p3.t24: Customers review terms and confirm their CPF taxpayer ID through the link; your team can verify acceptance using its hash and source.
capacidades.p3.t26: Your team prepares CCB (bank credit note), commercial note, debenture, loan agreement, and CPR (rural product note) documents for signing, with numbering and hashes to support verification.
capacidades.p4.t04: The institution links the payer's future inflows to the transaction and the fund; an active receivables lock is part of the disbursement conditions.
capacidades.p4.t06: Before releasing funds, the platform checks balances and single use of notes and remittances, linking collateral to the contract within the same transaction.
capacidades.p4.t08: The institution monitors the herd backing agricultural credit: tracking, animal health, liens, covenants, and agreements support ongoing collateral oversight.
capacidades.p4.t12: The desk tracks settlement confirmation to recognize payment; duplicate-payment controls protect the intended effect of disbursement authorization.
capacidades.p4.t14: Customers check balances, export statements, and make Pix payments using a key or QR code.
capacidades.p4.t16: Customers receive a boleto payment slip as a PDF; the desk issues the payment request, and reconciliation records settlement of the installment.
capacidades.p4.t18: Your team monitors obligations and records renegotiations, keeping agreements, covenants, and restrictions linked to the contract.
capacidades.p5.t03: At the desk, your team turns analysis and documentation into action: enabling, approving, and authorizing disbursement. Risk and oversight teams need the records that support this process.
common.c018: The assignor, with execution documents in view.
common.c022: The release of funds, authorized separately.
capacidades.p5.t07: The operator works through the queue, enables the assignor, and approves the transaction with execution documents in view. Disbursement authorization is available in the same workspace, with distinct actions for credit approval and release of funds.
capacidades.p5.t09: Your team monitors accounts, holds, and applications according to each user's role, with two-factor authentication for access.
capacidades.p5.t11: Risk and operations teams review records of approved and declined transactions within each organization's context.
capacidades.p5.t13: Support teams use operational identifiers; logs filter CPF and CNPJ taxpayer IDs, Pix keys, phone numbers, and email addresses.
capacidades.p5.t15: Teams reviewing the lending journey have access to 60 months of credit history and 36 months of execution history.
capacidades.p5.t17: Terms, acceptances, collateral, and audit records have a controlled source: protected records require server-signed writes.
capacidades.p5.t18: The FSB calls for records that “attribute actions … to specific agents.”<sup class="fn">4</sup>
capacidades.p5.t21: Gartner highlights modular, specialized agents “reusing proven solutions across workflows.”<sup class="fn">1</sup>
capacidades.p5.t23: The institution organizes products, policy, and workflows for each operation, bringing the foundations of the offering together in a vertical package.
capacidades.p5.t25: Each organization operates with its own data, keys, and events, preserving its operating context.
capacidades.p5.t27: Your product team combines identification, accounts, payments, signing, decisioning, calculations, audit trails, and conversation to design the chosen journey.
capacidades.p5.t29: Workflows coordinate recurring tasks and response waits, connecting triggers and dependencies across stages.
capacidades.p5.t31: Customers converse in their own language with agents using tools selected for the operation's context.
capacidades.p5.t33: Customers send and receive messages through WhatsApp, a channel that can be incorporated into your chosen journeys.

jornadas.p4.t23: Sent to the customer for payment.

arquitetura.p1.t06: For borrowers, the journey needs to connect the offer to contracting. For your team, it needs to connect underwriting, documents, and authorization.
arquitetura.p1.t07: The architecture starts with that journey: Catalisa's independent capabilities and vertical packages let you define each component's role in the offering.
arquitetura.p1.t08: Gartner highlights specialized agents “reusing proven solutions across workflows.”<sup class="fn">1</sup>
arquitetura.p2.t03: Customers move through receivables simulation, offer, and acceptance; the API connects the app to assessment. The risk team reviews policy and its sources; workflows coordinate dependencies and response waits.
arquitetura.p2.t04: Offer amounts, the signed document, and transaction records each have a distinct role in this journey.
arquitetura.p2.t09: The in-app customer journey, from simulation to tracking the accepted transaction.
arquitetura.p2.t10: The app with the bank's branding.

governanca-e-controles.p1.t01: Trust takes shape in the records.
governanca-e-controles.p1.t02: Understand decisions, verify contracting, and review credit history to support accountability for risk and operations.

governanca-e-controles.p2.t02: Those accountable for risk need to examine the criteria applied to credit and bring together transaction records for auditors and regulators.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t03: Versioned policy, decision paths, and audit trails for approved and declined transactions provide the material for that review.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t04: The FSB highlights “the impracticality of real-time human monitoring of agent decisions as their use scales” and calls for records and traceability of each action.<sup class="fn">4</sup>
governanca-e-controles.p2.t06: Your risk team expresses its criteria in versioned decision tables, connects data sources, and reviews the path to the outcome.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t07: The version identifies the policy under review; the trace shows how it was executed. This context supports the responsible team's review of the assessment.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t08: Policy in a decision table: publishing creates a new version.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t09: Gartner includes AI governance platforms in its AI TRiSM framework.<sup class="fn">7</sup>
governanca-e-controles.p2.t10: The desk puts human responsibility into practice.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t11: Your team accesses the queue, assignor enablement, execution documents, approval, and disbursement authorization at the credit desk.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t12: When a credit bureau response is still pending, the application goes to a person for review; conversational agents use tools selected for each organization.
governanca-e-controles.p2.t16: Each action has its own role in managing the contract.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t02: Customers sign through an email invitation and code confirmation; your team can verify execution using the sealed PDF and completion certificate.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t03: For assignments with linked counterparties, the transaction opens after server-side signature verification.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t04: Transaction acceptance confirmed with a selfie and recorded in the audit trail with the document code.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t07: Your team needs to trust the source of the records it reviews: terms, acceptances, collateral, and audit records require server-signed writes in protected collections.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t08: Console access is role-based, with two-factor authentication; each organization maintains its own data and event context.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t13: Credit history is retained for 60 months and execution history for 36 months, giving your team a defined review period for the journey.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t14: Teams investigating an event can use support identifiers; logs filter CPF and CNPJ taxpayer IDs, Pix keys, phone numbers, and email addresses.
governanca-e-controles.p3.t17: Your environment is part of the governance decision: on-premises in your environment or as SaaS.

notas.p1.t05: FSB, Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Final report, October 15, 2026.
